pr_title: HTS221: Check for drdy_gpio defs into DTS
pr_body:
Added the gpio for HTS221 drdy in Device Tree.
Fix #28443

Built only, not tested.
Issue here is because HTS221 has been added in build_all trigger file, but the gpio drdy was not provided in disco_l475_iot1 device tree.
I have not tested it on the board itself, I can do tomorrow if required. Please review also the schematic, I
may have an older one. Thanks!

EDIT:
Totally changed the fix. Instead of defining the drdy_gpios in DTS (it is a not required option) I check it in the hts221 driver itself before using the generated macro.
pr_comments:
@pabigot 
I think they should remain separated because, in case of multi-instance (sooner or later I will introduce it in HTS221), we need to check the presence of drdy_gpios instance by instance. How can we do that?

Probably we need some filter that currently is not existing.

What about

    #define HTS221_TRIGGER_ENABLED(inst) (DT_INST_NODE_HAS_PROP(inst, drdy_gpios) && IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_HTS221_TRIGGER))

@pabigot 
See for example the current lsm6dsl.c, it is a multi-instance and we have exactly the same issue, i.e. if irq_gpios is not defined in DT then the build fails. How can we change that code? I was thinking to do a change similar to what I'm proposing here, but again there should be a better way.

> I think they should remain separated because, in case of multi-instance (sooner or later I will introduce it in HTS221), we need to check the presence of drdy_gpios instance by instance. How can we do that?

Yeah, OK.  I was proposing a path that would get #28443 fixed for 2.4.0.

For multi instance the preprocessor check is solely dependent on `CONFIG_HTS221_TRIGGER`, and the runtime check looks for a non-null DRDY device name.  Then the instantiation macros use `COND_CODE_1()` to check for the devicetree property to conditionally initialize the configuration structure fields related to the GPIO.  Something like this:
```
``
#ifdef CONFIG_LSM6DSL_TRIGGER
#define LSM6DSL_CFG_IRQ(inst) \
                .irq_dev_name = DT_INST_GPIO_LABEL(inst, irq_gpios),    \
                .irq_pin = DT_INST_GPIO_PIN(inst, irq_gpios),           \
                .irq_flags = DT_INST_GPIO_FLAGS(inst, irq_gpios),
#else
#define LSM6DSL_CFG_IRQ(inst)
#endif

#define LSM6DSL_CONFIG_I2C(inst)                                        \
        {                                                               \
                .bus_name = DT_INST_BUS_LABEL(inst),                    \
                .bus_init = lsm6dsl_i2c_init,                           \
                .bus_cfg = { .i2c_slv_addr = DT_INST_REG_ADDR(inst), }, \
		COND_CODE_1(DT_INST_HAS_PROP(inst, irq_gpios),          \
		            (CONFIG_LSMDSL_TRIGGER(inst)),())           \
        }
```

Note this gets rid of the duplication of the non-conditional initialization which cleans the code up nicely (you don't need two versions of `LSM6DSL_CONFIG_I2C` based on `CONFIG_LSM6DSL_TRIGGER`).

Does that make sense?

> > I think they should remain separated because, in case of multi-instance (sooner or later I will introduce it in HTS221), we need to check the presence of drdy_gpios instance by instance. How can we do that?
> 
> Yeah, OK. I was proposing a path that would get #28443 fixed for 2.4.0.
> 
> For multi instance the preprocessor check is solely dependent on `CONFIG_HTS221_TRIGGER`, and the runtime check looks for a non-null DRDY device name. Then the instantiation macros use `COND_CODE_1()` to check for the devicetree property to conditionally initialize the configuration structure fields related to the GPIO. Something like this:
> 
> ```
> ``
> #ifdef CONFIG_LSM6DSL_TRIGGER
> #define LSM6DSL_CFG_IRQ(inst) \
>                 .irq_dev_name = DT_INST_GPIO_LABEL(inst, irq_gpios),    \
>                 .irq_pin = DT_INST_GPIO_PIN(inst, irq_gpios),           \
>                 .irq_flags = DT_INST_GPIO_FLAGS(inst, irq_gpios),
> #else
> #define LSM6DSL_CFG_IRQ(inst)
> #endif
> 
> #define LSM6DSL_CONFIG_I2C(inst)                                        \
>         {                                                               \
>                 .bus_name = DT_INST_BUS_LABEL(inst),                    \
>                 .bus_init = lsm6dsl_i2c_init,                           \
>                 .bus_cfg = { .i2c_slv_addr = DT_INST_REG_ADDR(inst), }, \
> 		COND_CODE_1(DT_INST_HAS_PROP(inst, irq_gpios),          \
> 		            (CONFIG_LSMDSL_TRIGGER(inst)),())           \
>         }
> ```
> 
> Note this gets rid of the duplication of the non-conditional initialization which cleans the code up nicely (you don't need two versions of `LSM6DSL_CONFIG_I2C` based on `CONFIG_LSM6DSL_TRIGGER`).
> 
> Does that make sense?

Yes it does.
I need time to make changes here, but definetely makes sense.
Thanks
Approved now to remove any delay for re-review after this is updated to pass CI.  I don't expect those changes to be a problem.

> Looks good, though there's still some reference that isn't getting excluded causing the build failures. So will approve once it passes CI.

Yeah, thanks.
A couple of silly mistakes in trigger file. But nothing too serious. Should pass now.

review_comments: Shouldn't we add a check to be sure that `drdy_gpios` is present when `CONFIG_HTS221_TRIGGER` is enabled?

I don't think so.  The Kconfig signals that support for the trigger should be present in the driver.  That support doesn't require that the signal actually be present in the hardware.  (It might not be in a shield, and the application should get a runtime error if it the code tries to use something that isn't supported by the hardware.)

We probably don't have any policy on that, so I suppose we could start to require that if the driver enables interrupts the hardware must provide support for them.  I don't think that's a good idea, though.
